output.summary: The PR changes the bounds check in src/bounds.ts from `index < length` to `index <= length`, which breaks the documented contract that valid integer indices are 0 through length-1 and that empty collections have no valid index. This is a correctness regression that causes out-of-bounds indices to be accepted.

findings.title: Off-by-one: index equal to length is incorrectly considered in-bounds
findings.body: inBounds now returns true when `index === length`. For nonnegative integer length, the largest valid index is `length-1`, so `index === length` is out of bounds. This also makes empty collections (length 0) report `index 0` as in-bounds. The change therefore fails the frozen acceptance counterexamples (index=3,length=3 expected false but observed true; index=0,length=0 expected false but observed true) and breaks callers that rely on this function to guard array indexing.
findings.evidence: src/bounds.ts line 2 reads `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. The synthetic CI counterexamples report {index:3,length:3} observed true (expected false) and {index:0,length:0} observed true (expected false).
findings.suggestion: Restore the strict upper bound: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`.

output.diagnosis: The diff changed the upper-bound comparison operator from `<` to `<=`, an off-by-one error that permits `index === length` to be treated as valid, contradicting the public contract that valid indices are 0 through length-1.
